title: Console route activity enriched catalog and normalized event schema
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Problem: Current Console analytics consumers (dashboard, cost allocation, alerting) stitch together multiple narrow event tables (route_events, token_logs, session_meta) in ad-hoc SQL. This leads to expensive joins, inconsistent dimensions (tenant_id, route_path normalization), and divergent interpretations across teams. We need a single curated, query-ready table (console_route_activity_enriched) that serves most downstream needs and is easy to join for ad-hoc analysis.

Goal: Design, implement, and backfill a normalized event/enrichment schema and produce a curated materialized table named console_route_activity_enriched with the following properties:
- Tenant-aware: tenant_id and workspace_id canonicalized; supports anonymous workspace mapping.
- Route normalization: canonical_route_id, route_path_template, route_metadata (category, owner) resolved from config service snapshot.
- Enriched fields: user_id (nullable), session_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, response_time_ms, response_status, prefix_cache_hit (bool), batch_size, cost_estimate_usd.
- Time and partitioning: event_timestamp (utc), partitioned by event_date (DATE), clustered by tenant_id, canonical_route_id.
- Update semantics: incremental daily materialized view refreshed hourly with late-arriving window of 72 hours applied via SCD-2 style dedup/upsert using event_id.
- Storage/perf: Parquet/ORC on BigLake, columns compressed, use low-cardinality encoding for model_variant, route_template.

Design Decisions / Trade-offs:
- Denormalize route metadata to avoid repeated joins vs keep small lookup table. We opt to denormalize snapshot at enrichment time to reduce query cost for dashboards.
- Use hourly incremental refresh to keep dashboards near-real-time but bound compute costs; backfill job handles historical ingestion.
- Cost estimate computed heuristically based on tokens and pricing profiles; flagged as "estimated_cost_usd" to avoid being treated as billing-grade.

Implementation Plan:
1) Define normalized raw schema (console_events_raw) and lightweight ETL to parse ingress payloads and standardize fields.
   - Owner: data-ingest team (ENG-40123 dependency)
   - Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Analytics/Normalized+Console+Event+Schema (draft)
2) Enrichment job: join raw events with config snapshots (route catalog) and token logs to produce console_route_activity_staging.
   - Use Spark job with autoscaling cluster; use TTL of 14 days for staging.
3) Materialized curated table: implement as incremental merge job (MERGE INTO) to build console_route_activity_enriched partitioned by event_date.
   - Initial backfill strategy: parallel date-range backfills with small windowed checkpoints to limit rewrite. Estimated two days of cluster time for historical 12 months.
4) Downstream migration: update dashboards (Looker/Grafana), costing jobs, console SLO rollups to point at the new table. Provide compatibility views for deprecated tables for 90 days.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Unit tests for enrichment logic and cost heuristics.
- Backfill completes for last 12 months in staging and sample dashboards validate numbers.
- Console dashboards load 50% faster on average for common queries (measured via perf tests).
- All known consumers migrated or have migration plan documented.

Artifacts and PRs:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Analytics/Console+Route+Enriched+Catalog+Design (linked)
- Draft SQL snippets (examples below)
  Example incremental MERGE:
  MERGE INTO analytics.console_route_activity_enriched T
  USING staging.console_route_activity_staging S
  ON T.event_id = S.event_id
  WHEN MATCHED AND S.updated_at > T.updated_at THEN UPDATE SET *
  WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *;

- GitHub PR (work-in-progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/1429

Rollout / Migration Plan:
- Phase 1 (This ticket): schema + enrichment + initial daily incremental pipeline in staging.
- Phase 2: backfill 12 months into staging, validate dashboards.
- Phase 3: rename and swap readers in a single maintenance window; keep compatibility view for 90 days.

Monitoring / Observability:
- Pipeline metrics: row counts, lag (max event_timestamp delay), merge conflicts, hourly cost (compute).
- Alerting: job failures, merge rate anomalies (>20% failure).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize cost heuristic for multi-model requests (ask Product for expected pricing profiles).
- Confirm long-term retention policy for enriched table (default 2 years) with compliance.

Notes: This ticket focuses exclusively on the curated/enriched table and its ingestion pipeline. Separate follow-ups will handle per-token billing-grade reconciliation and console-internal SDK changes to emit normalized event ids.
